ideas: Plastic bags pollute oceans and last for centuries
Easy alternatives already exist and people adapt quickly
Some exceptions for hygiene or medical use

phrases.phrase: take hundreds of years to break down

phrases.meaning: animals and plants living in the sea

model: Yes, I think plastic bags should be banned entirely, although it would be sensible to phase them out over a year or two. First, they cause huge environmental damage. Most plastic bags are used for about twenty minutes, but they take hundreds of years to break down, and a lot of them end up in rivers and the sea. When I visited a beach in Quang Ngai last summer, there were bags tangled in the rocks everywhere, and it's well known that they harm marine life like turtles. Another reason is that the alternatives are cheap and easy. If shops stopped giving out bags tomorrow, people would simply carry a cloth bag or use a box. My local supermarket began charging for bags last year, and within a few weeks most customers had got used to bringing their own. It's really only a small inconvenience. If the government bans them, I'm sure it will change people's habits very quickly. So overall, a full ban is the most effective solution.
